content.short: Cartesi is an application-specific rollup protocol with a Linux runtime.
content.description: EVM programmability constraints impose heavy computational and design limits on DApp developers. Cartesi’s RISC-V virtual machine enables building complex, compute-intensive DApps with familiar libraries, compilers, and other time-tested open-source tooling. Cartesi rollups can be deployed as Layer 2 on Ethereum, Layer 3 on Optimism or Arbitrum, zkEVM chains, or used as sovereign rollups, expanding where and how scalable, verifiable smart contracts and off-chain logic can run and be settled on chain.

resources.title: Why a Linux-Based Execution Layer Changes What DeFi Can Build
resources.tldr: Argues the EVM imposes a structural ceiling and a real Linux runtime onchain lifts it. Makes the constraint concrete rather than gesturing at scale.
